tools.name: list_permit_trails
tools.description: List the Madeira trails that need a government hiking permit for a set start time and can be reserved on madeira.fun. Returns each trail's seo_slug (use it in the other tools), code (such as PR 18 or PS PR 1), name, island, official trail status, trail page and day feed links. Optional query filters

tools.name: get_permit_fees
tools.description: The government hiking permit fee records in force today (format MF-PRC-1.0, the same records as https://madeira.fun/hiking/permit-data), with legal references and exemptions. Give trail to get the fee that applies to that trail. The fee is paid to the government, never to madeira.fun.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_start_times" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_reservation" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Step 1 of 2 to reserve a Madeira hiking permit for a visitor through madeira.fun. Before calling, tell the visitor these three points in your own words and get …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_permit_trails, start_reservation · Private data: get_permit_fees · Public sink: start_reservation, confirm_reservation · Destructive: get_permit_fees.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_permit_trails, start_reservation · Private data: get_permit_fees · Public sink: start_reservation, confirm_reservation · Destructive: get_permit_fees

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
